Completed onboarding with Renato. He was very friendly throughout the conversation and asked several detailed questions regarding the program and approval requirements for customers. I explained that EasyPay reviews multiple factors during the approval process, including credit history, income, recent credit activity, debt-to-income ratio, prior defaults, and ensuring the customer’s bank account has been active for at least 90 days.

I also emphasized the importance of tax exemption and ensuring taxes are not included on invoices, as EasyPay collects taxes directly from the customer. Additionally, we reviewed the requirement that all transactions must be completed in person, since EasyPay does not support online transactions.

We also discussed best practices for processing the $39 fee. Overall, Renato demonstrated a strong understanding of the process, especially since he already works with several financing providers such as Asima, Cfna, Snap Finance, and Progressive Leasing.

Subject: 00TTO00000vruCv2AI
Full Comments:
Completed onboarding with Anna. She had minimal questions throughout the training. One of her main questions was regarding what an ITIN number is, and I explained that it is a tax identification number used for customers who do not have legal status or a Social Security number. I also emphasized the importance of verifying that these customers provide a valid Texas-issued or government-issued ID.

Overall, Anna demonstrated a clear understanding of the process. I highlighted the importance of marking invoices as tax exempt, explaining that EasyPay collects taxes directly from the customer so the shop does not have to. I also stressed the importance of verifying IDs and ensuring that all transactions are completed in person.

Anna mentioned that the process seemed very easy and straightforward. I made sure to provide her with my contact information in case any questions or concerns arise. She also mentioned that she may be submitting or finalizing her first application today.
